common_name: Red Pepper Azalea (Fragrant Orange-Red Native Hybrid Azalea, 2008 ARS Azalea of the Year)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; this upright Aromi hybrid was named the American Rhododendron Society's Rhododendron of the Year in 2008.

directions: Red Pepper is a Dr. Eugene Aromi hybrid bred from 'Gallipoli' and Rhododendron austrinum, chosen as the American Rhododendron Society's Rhododendron of the Year in 2008. Buds open strong red before flaring into brilliant orange-yellow trumpets heavily flushed with vivid red, held in lightly fragrant, ball-shaped trusses that cover the plant in a heavy spring flush. The floriferous, upright shrub reaches roughly 6 feet tall and 3 feet wide within a decade and tolerates both Gulf Coast heat and winter cold to around 10 degrees F. Plant in humus-rich, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade, and mulch to keep the shallow roots cool and evenly moist through summer.
sources: The Azalean (2003) — Named Aromi Deciduous Hybrids chart

common_name: Pathfinder Azalea (Fragrant Golden Native Hybrid Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; this early, vigorous Aromi hybrid later served as a parent of 'Jane's Gold.'

directions: Pathfinder is an early Dr. Eugene Aromi hybrid from a 'Rothschild Orange' seedling crossed with Rhododendron austrinum, registered in 1996 by Magnolia Nursery of Chunchula, Alabama. Orange buds unfurl into fragrant golden flowers deepened by a bold gold blotch, produced in heavy spring trusses on a vigorous, upright shrub. It later served as a parent of 'Jane's Gold,' passing on its golden color and fragrance to further Aromi introductions. Grow in humus-rich, acidic, evenly moist soil in partial shade, and mulch well to protect the shallow roots through hot Gulf Coast summers.
sources: The Azalean (2003) — Named Aromi Deciduous Hybrids chart

common_name: Jane's Gold Azalea (Fragrant Cream-Gold Native Hybrid Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in rich, moist, acidic, well-drained soil in part sun to light shade.

directions: Jane's Gold is a Dr. Eugene Aromi hybrid from 'Pathfinder' crossed with 'Golden Sunset,' producing abundant clusters of spicy-sweet-scented cream-gold flowers with a strong yellow-orange blotch and petal tips lightly flushed rose. Orange-tipped buds open in early to mid-spring on a shrub that typically reaches 6 to 8 feet tall and 4 to 6 feet wide at maturity. Like other Aromi hybrids it draws Gulf Coast heat and humidity tolerance from its native azalea parentage. Plant in part sun to light shade in rich, moist, acidic, well-drained soil, and mulch to keep roots cool through summer.
sources: The Azalean (2003) — Named Aromi Deciduous Hybrids chart

common_name: Tensaw Azalea (Fragrant Bright Yellow Native Hybrid Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade.

directions: Tensaw is a Dr. Eugene Aromi hybrid from Rhododendron austrinum crossed with 'Oxydol,' bearing fragrant bright yellow flowers roughly two inches across in a heavy spring flush. Like other austrinum-derived Aromi introductions, it combines Gulf Coast heat and humidity tolerance with strong fragrance on a medium-sized, multi-stemmed shrub. Grow in humus-rich, acidic, evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial shade, and mulch well to protect the shallow root system through summer heat. It produces a profuse early-to-mid-spring bloom typical of the austrinum breeding line.
sources: The Azalean (2003) — Named Aromi Deciduous Hybrids chart

common_name: Fool's Folly Azalea (Fragrant Yellow-Orange Native Hybrid Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; this Aromi hybrid was later used as a parent of 'Centerpiece.'

directions: Fool's Folly is a Dr. Eugene Aromi hybrid from a 'Rothschild Orange' seedling crossed with Rhododendron austrinum, with orange buds opening into bright yellow flowers lightly flushed orange. It was later used as a parent of 'Centerpiece,' passing its yellow coloring into a line of white- and cream-flowered Aromi descendants. The shrub carries the fragrance, heat tolerance, and vigor typical of austrinum-derived Aromi hybrids on a medium, rounded habit. Plant in humus-rich, acidic, evenly moist soil in partial shade, and mulch well to protect the shallow roots through hot summers.
sources: The Azalean (2003) — Named Aromi Deciduous Hybrids chart

common_name: Forty-niner Azalea (Fragrant Golden Native Hybrid Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; this Aromi hybrid was later used as a parent of 'Frontier Red.'

directions: Forty-niner is a Dr. Eugene Aromi hybrid from a 'Rothschild Orange' seedling crossed with Rhododendron austrinum, bearing golden flowers brushed with a scarlet flush at the petal edges. It was later used as a parent of 'Frontier Red,' passing on its bold two-tone coloring to further Aromi introductions. The upright shrub blooms in a heavy spring flush and shares the fragrance and Gulf Coast heat tolerance common to austrinum-derived Aromi hybrids. Grow in humus-rich, acidic, evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial shade, and mulch to protect the shallow root system through summer heat.
sources: The Azalean (2003) — Named Aromi Deciduous Hybrids chart

common_name: Lacecap Azalea (Pink Flat-Truss Native Hybrid Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in humus-rich, acidic soil that stays consistently moist, in partial shade to filtered sun.

directions: Lacecap is a Dr. Eugene Aromi hybrid from Rhododendron viscosum crossed with a dark red Ilam azalea, producing light pink, white-flushed flowers that open wide in a distinctive flat truss rather than the rounded ball-shaped trusses typical of most Aromi hybrids. Its swamp azalea parentage brings a later, early-summer bloom time and a preference for consistently moist soil, setting it apart from the more drought-tolerant austrinum-derived side of the breeding line. The shrub forms a medium, multi-stemmed clump well suited to the damp margins of a woodland garden or pond edge. Plant in humus-rich, acidic soil that stays evenly moist, in partial shade to filtered sun.
sources: The Azalean (2003) — Named Aromi Deciduous Hybrids chart

common_name: Tradewinds Azalea (Fragrant Light Yellow Native Hybrid Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade.

directions: Tradewinds is a Dr. Eugene Aromi hybrid from Rhododendron austrinum crossed with 'George Reynolds,' bearing very fragrant, large light yellow flowers lightly flushed orange. The vigorous shrub produces a heavy spring flush of blooms and shares the Gulf Coast heat and humidity tolerance typical of austrinum-derived Aromi introductions. It grows into an upright, multi-stemmed habit well suited to a woodland-edge border or mixed shrub planting. Grow in humus-rich, acidic, evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial shade, and mulch to protect the shallow root system through summer heat.
sources: The Azalean (2003) — Named Aromi Deciduous Hybrids chart

common_name: Centerpiece Azalea (Fragrant White-Gold Native Hybrid Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; this Aromi hybrid became an important parent of later white- and cream-flowered introductions.

directions: Centerpiece is a Dr. Eugene Aromi hybrid from 'Fool's Folly' crossed with 'Elmer's Yellow,' opening from light cream buds into white flowers brightened by a deep yellow blotch. It became an important parent in its own right, used to breed a line of later Aromi introductions including 'High Tide,' 'Peach Glow,' and 'Moon Dreams.' The shrub blooms in a heavy spring flush and carries the fragrance and Gulf Coast heat tolerance typical of the Aromi breeding line. Plant in humus-rich, acidic, evenly moist soil in partial shade, and mulch to protect the shallow roots through summer heat.
sources: The Azalean (2003) — Named Aromi Deciduous Hybrids chart
